o: Explain the effects of clock speed, cache size and number of CPU cores on CPU performance.
Use exam command words to explain each factor accurately in context.
Calculate clock cycles using valid OCR Exam Reference Language.
refs: L018 / L010 · image size and compression
r: What is stored by the Program Counter (PC), and what is held in the Memory Data Register (MDR)?
PC: address of the next instruction to be fetched. MDR: the data or instruction currently being transferred to/from memory. Both are registers.
Identify one job of the ALU and one job of the Control Unit.
ALU: arithmetic and logical operations. Control Unit: decodes instructions and coordinates/controls CPU activity.
Convert 4 KB to bytes using the decimal convention 1 KB = 1,000 bytes.
A 120 × 80 pixel image uses 8-bit colour depth. Calculate the uncompressed pixel-data size in bytes. Why should a source-code file use lossless rather than lossy compression?
120 × 80 = 9,600 pixels. × 8 = 76,800 bits. ÷ 8 = 9,600 bytes. Lossless is required to restore the original source code exactly.
c: Clock speed is measured in hertz (Hz): clock cycles per second. 1 GHz is one billion cycles per second. A higher clock speed generally allows the CPU to progress through more work per second. A cycle is NOT necessarily one finished instruction.

Cache is small, fast memory close to or within the CPU. It holds frequently used data and instructions. Increasing cache size can mean fewer slower main-memory (RAM) accesses, improving performance in workloads that benefit.
A CPU may have multiple cores. Different threads or tasks can execute in parallel on separate cores, improving multitasking. Additional cores do not guarantee a faster single-threaded task.
Write: factor → mechanism → performance consequence. For example, larger cache → more frequently accessed instructions stay close to CPU → fewer slower RAM reads → faster execution in suitable tasks.

m.q: A school PC runs multiple applications while pupils edit video. Explain how a larger cache and additional CPU cores may improve performance. [4 marks]
st: Identify the two factors in the question: cache size and core count. Plan two explained points, each worth up to two marks.
Larger cache stores more frequently used instructions and data near the CPU [1]. This can reduce slower main-memory accesses and improve processing speed [1].
Additional cores can process separate tasks or threads at the same time [1]. This may improve multitasking while pupils run several applications [1].
Review all four points against the command word 'explain'. Avoid claiming that twice as many cores automatically doubles speed.

w: A processor runs at 3 GHz for 2 seconds. Calculate clock cycles and explain why the value is NOT necessarily the number of instructions executed.
3 billion cycles per second × 2 seconds = 6 billion clock cycles. One instruction can use more or fewer cycles; actual throughput depends on the CPU and workload.
Explain in two linked points how larger cache size may improve CPU performance. [2 marks]
Cache holds more frequently used data/instructions close to the CPU [1]; this reduces the need to fetch these from slower RAM [1].
Two pupils use the same computer. One runs a single-threaded program; the other runs several independent programs. Which is likely to benefit more from extra cores, and why?
Several independent programs may use different cores in parallel. A strictly single-threaded program may not use extra cores, so speedup is not guaranteed.

k.q: Predict, change and extend this complete OCR ERL program. Work on your whiteboard first; then check it in the OCR ERL editor.
k.code:
clockGHz = 2
seconds = 3
cyclesBillions = clockGHz * seconds
print(cyclesBillions)
p: Predict the output and state exactly what the number represents.
Change clockGHz to 3 and seconds to 4. Predict the output, then check.
Extend the program to print the total number of cycles (not billions): multiply cyclesBillions by 1000000000. Explain why this does not calculate completed instructions.
k.a: Original output: 6 (six billion clock cycles). With 3 GHz and 4 seconds: 12. Add cycles = cyclesBillions * 1000000000 followed by print(cycles); this displays 12000000000. Clock cycles do not equal instructions completed.

e: Explain how the number of CPU cores affects performance. [3 marks] (From your Paper 1 revision booklet, 1.1.2, exam-question practice.)

Multiple CPU cores allow separate tasks or threads to be processed at the same time (parallel processing) [1]. This can improve multitasking [1] and increase processing throughput where the software can use multiple cores [1]. Do not claim every program becomes proportionally faster.
A school is replacing a CPU with one having a larger cache. Explain two ways cache improves access to frequently used instructions. [4 marks] (Original J277-style application question.)

Cache is fast memory near the CPU [1]. It stores frequently accessed instructions/data [1]. Larger cache can retain more of these items [1], reducing slower main-memory access and helping performance [1]. A valid linked explanation earns the relevant marks.
Explain how clock speed, cache size and number of cores affect CPU performance. [6 marks] (From your Paper 1 revision booklet, 1.1.2, exam-question practice.)

Clock speed: number of cycles per second [1], higher speeds can allow processing to progress faster [1]. Cache: more frequently used data/instructions available quickly [1], reducing access to slower RAM [1]. Cores: more independent instructions/threads/tasks can run in parallel [1], improving throughput/multitasking for suitable workloads [1].
v: Number of clock cycles per second, measured in hertz (Hz).
Unit of frequency; one cycle per second.
Small, fast memory close to or in the CPU containing frequently used data and instructions.
Processing unit capable of executing instructions, potentially independently of other cores.
Running separate tasks or threads at the same time on multiple processing units.
A limiting factor holding back overall performance.
x: Doubling the number of CPU cores always makes every program twice as fast.
